question: On October 31, India celebrates which day to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Unity Day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Unity Day (राष्ट्रीय एकता दिवस) is observed on 31 October every year to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister of India.

• It was first introduced by the Government of India in 2014.

• Sardar Patel is remembered as the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating over 560 princely states into the Indian Union.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Statue of Unity in Gujarat (world's tallest statue at 182 m) is dedicated to Sardar Patel.

• On this day, the 'Run for Unity' is organised across the country.

NOTE

• National Science Day (Option 1): Observed on 28 February to mark the discovery of the Raman Effect by C.V. Raman.

• National Martyrs' Day (Option 2): Observed on 30 January (martyrdom of Mahatma Gandhi) and also on 23 March (Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev).

• National Constitution Day (Option 4): Observed on 26 November to mark the adoption of the Constitution in 1949.

question: Who took over as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in December 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Malhotra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanjay Malhotra took charge as the 26th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक के गवर्नर) in December 2024.

• He is a 1990-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre and earlier served as Revenue Secretary.

• He succeeded Shaktikanta Das, whose extended term ended in December 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The RBI Governor is appointed by the Central Government and heads the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.

NOTE

• Shaktikanta Das (Option 1): The 25th RBI Governor (2018–2024), whom Sanjay Malhotra succeeded.

• Raghuram Rajan (Option 2): The 23rd RBI Governor (2013–2016), noted economist.

• Urjit Patel (Option 3): The 24th RBI Governor (2016–2018).

question: In May 2025, Anurag Bhushan has been appointed as the India's next Ambassador to ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sweden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2025, senior diplomat Anurag Bhushan was appointed as India's next Ambassador to the Kingdom of Sweden (स्वीडन).

• He is an officer of the Indian Foreign Service (IFS).

• The appointment was announced by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The capital of Sweden is Stockholm and its currency is the Swedish Krona.

• India and Sweden share strong ties in innovation, clean technology and trade.

NOTE

• Denmark (Option 1): Nordic country with capital Copenhagen; not the posting here.

• Australia (Option 3): Capital Canberra; India's High Commissioner, not Ambassador, serves there.

• Canada (Option 4): Capital Ottawa; also headed by a High Commissioner.

question: The Union Budget 2025-26 states that total number of students in 23 IITs has increased 100 per cent from 65,000 to 1.35 lakh in the past ____ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Union Budget 2025-26 (केंद्रीय बजट 2025-26), the total number of students in the 23 IITs has increased 100 per cent from 65,000 to 1.35 lakh in the past 10 years.

• The Budget also proposed additional infrastructure in five IITs started after 2014 to accommodate 6,500 more students.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2025.

• The first IIT was established at Kharagpur in 1951.

NOTE

• 8 (Option 2): Not the figure mentioned in the Budget document.

• 20 (Option 3): Incorrect; overstates the period cited.

• 5 (Option 4): Incorrect; the growth was measured over a decade, not five years.

question:
The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025 aims to:
I. Abolish Waqf board completely
II. Streamline the management of Waqf properties
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025 (वक्फ (संशोधन) विधेयक 2025) aims to streamline the management of Waqf properties, improve transparency and efficiency in administration.

• It does not abolish the Waqf Board; rather it reforms its functioning.

• Hence only statement II is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Bill seeks to enhance the role of the Central Waqf Council and State Waqf Boards through better record-keeping and digitisation.

• Waqf refers to property permanently dedicated for religious or charitable purposes under Islamic law.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, as the Bill does not abolish the Waqf board.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since statement I is incorrect.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, since statement II is correct.

question: In July 2025, ______ launched a national level initiative SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness)
option_3: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2025, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (कौशल विकास और उद्यमिता मंत्रालय) launched the national-level initiative SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness).

• SOAR aims to prepare students and youth with Artificial Intelligence skills for future readiness.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was formed in 2014.

• It runs the flagship Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

NOTE

• Ministry of Education (Option 1): Handles school and higher education policy, not this initiative.

• Ministry of Electronics & IT (Option 2): Deals with digital and IT infrastructure and IndiaAI Mission.

• Ministry of Science & Technology (Option 4): Oversees scientific research through DST, DSIR and DBT.

question: The Export Preparedness Index India is developed by ____.
option_1: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Export Preparedness Index (EPI) (निर्यात तैयारी सूचकांक) for India is developed by NITI Aayog.

• It is a data-driven index that assesses the export readiness and performance of Indian states and union territories.

• It is prepared in collaboration with the Institute of Competitiveness.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

• Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister of India.

NOTE

• Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Option 1): Focuses on IT and digital governance, not this index.

• Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Option 2): No such ministry name; India has the Ministry of External Affairs handling diplomacy.

• CSIR (Option 4): Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, a scientific research body.

question: The natural host of the Nipah Virus is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fruit Bats.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The natural host (reservoir) of the Nipah Virus (निपाह वायरस) is the fruit bat of the genus Pteropus (also called flying foxes).

• The virus can spread to humans through contaminated food or direct contact with infected bats or animals.

• Nipah is a zoonotic disease with a high fatality rate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nipah Virus was first identified in 1998–99 in Malaysia and Singapore.

• In India, outbreaks have been reported mainly in Kerala.

NOTE

• Mosquitoes (Option 1): Vectors for malaria, dengue and chikungunya, not Nipah.

• Pigs (Option 3): Act as intermediate/amplifying hosts, not the natural reservoir.

• Sand Flies (Option 4): Transmit leishmaniasis (kala-azar), not Nipah.

question: Which of the following state government has planned to develop Jhajjar-Bachauli wildlife sanctuary as 1st leopard safari destination in the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Punjab (पंजाब) government has planned to develop the Jhajjar-Bachauli Wildlife Sanctuary as the first leopard safari destination in the state.

• The sanctuary is located in the Ropar (Rupnagar) district near the Shivalik foothills.

• The initiative is part of the state's plan to promote eco-tourism, alongside developing Nangal as a tourist hub.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The capital of Punjab (shared with Haryana) is Chandigarh.

• Punjab's other notable wildlife sanctuaries include Harike, Bir Motibagh and Abohar.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for the Gir National Park (Asiatic lions), not this project.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Not associated with the Jhajjar-Bachauli sanctuary.

• Telangana (Option 4): Not the state undertaking this leopard safari plan.

question: The Mishras of Bettiah Gharana, renowned for Dhrupad singing, are associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bettiah Gharana, renowned for Dhrupad singing (ध्रुपद गायन), is associated with Bettiah in the West Champaran district of Bihar.

• The Mishra family are the traditional custodians of this Dhrupad style.

• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of Hindustani classical vocal music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bettiah Gharana received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag for its Dhrupad tradition.

• The capital of Bihar is Patna.

NOTE

• Telangana (Option 2): Known for Perini Shivatandavam dance; not linked to Bettiah Gharana.

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Known for folk forms like Jhora and Chholiya, not this gharana.

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Associated with Natya Sangeet and Lavani, not Bettiah Dhrupad.

question: The Gwalior Fort, was initiated by ____ who finished the fortification system around the plateau in 773CE.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Sourya Sena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gwalior Fort (ग्वालियर किला) is traditionally believed to have been initiated by Raja Suraj Sen (Sourya Sena), who completed the fortification around the plateau in 773 CE.

• According to legend, the sage Gwalipa cured Suraj Sen of leprosy, and the city and fort were named after him.

• The fort is located in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gwalior Fort is often called the 'Gibraltar of India'.

• It houses the Man Singh Palace, built by Raja Man Singh Tomar, and the Teli ka Mandir.

NOTE

• Akbar (Option 1): Mughal emperor (1556–1605); did not initiate the fort.

• Rana Sanga (Option 2): Rajput ruler of Mewar; not the founder of Gwalior Fort.

• Ashoka (Option 4): Mauryan emperor; not associated with the fort's construction.

question: 'Spao' is a warrior dance performed in which of the following Indian state/Union Territory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Spao' (स्पाओ) is a traditional warrior dance performed in the Union Territory of Ladakh.

• It depicts the valour and heroism of warriors and is performed to martial music.

• It reflects Ladakh's rich cultural and martial heritage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019.

• Other famous dances of Ladakh include Jabro, Chham and Shondol.

NOTE

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Known for Charkula, Kathak and Raslila, not Spao.

• Bihar (Option 3): Known for Jat-Jatin and Bidesia folk dances.

• Puducherry (Option 4): Known for Garadi and other folk performances.

question: In April 2025, which country has launched the 'Three Gorges Antarctic Eye' telescope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2025, China (चीन) launched the 'Three Gorges Antarctic Eye' telescope.

• It is a terahertz telescope installed in Antarctica to observe the atmosphere and study climate and astronomical phenomena.

• The project is named after China's Three Gorges area.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The capital of China is Beijing and its currency is the Renminbi (Yuan).

• China operates several research stations in Antarctica, including Zhongshan and Qinling.

NOTE

• Russia (Option 2): Operates Antarctic stations like Vostok but did not launch this telescope.

• India (Option 3): Runs Maitri and Bharati stations in Antarctica; not linked to this project.

• United States (Option 4): Operates the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station, not this telescope.

question: Which IIT launched India's First hyper loop test track in March 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIT Madras.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• IIT Madras (आई.आई.टी. मद्रास) launched India's first Hyperloop test track in March 2025.

• The 410-metre test facility was developed by the Avishkar Hyperloop team in collaboration with Indian Railways and TuTr Hyperloop.

• Hyperloop is a high-speed transport technology using pods in low-pressure tubes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• IIT Madras was established in 1959 with German collaboration.

• It has consistently topped the NIRF rankings among Indian institutions.

NOTE

• IIT Bombay (Option 1): Established in 1958; not associated with this Hyperloop track.

• IIT Kanpur (Option 3): Known for aerospace and flight-testing research, not this project.

• IIT Delhi (Option 4): A leading IIT but not the one that built the Hyperloop track.

question: When a company hires regular service from external sources which was previously provided internally is known as ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Outsourcing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Outsourcing (आउटसोर्सिंग) is the practice where a company hires regular services from external sources that were previously provided internally.

• It helps firms reduce costs and focus on core competencies.

• Common examples include Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), IT services and customer support.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India is a leading global hub for outsourcing, especially in the IT and BPO sectors.

• Outsourcing became prominent with the growth of globalisation in the 1990s.

NOTE

• Subsidization (Option 2): Providing financial support (subsidy) to reduce costs of a good or service.

• Cross-Subsidization (Option 3): Charging higher prices to one group to subsidise lower prices for another.

• Globalisation (Option 4): The integration of economies through trade, capital and technology flows.

question: Under which of the following governor-General a new policy of "paramountcy" was initiated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Hastings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The policy of 'Paramountcy' (सर्वोच्चता / परामउंटसी) was initiated under Lord Hastings (Governor-General 1813–1823).

• Under this policy, the British East India Company claimed supremacy, asserting that its authority was paramount over all Indian states.

• It laid the foundation for the later doctrine of British political supremacy in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lord Hastings defeated the Marathas in the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–1818).

• The paramountcy policy was later expanded by Lord Dalhousie.

NOTE

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 2): Introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793) and civil service reforms.

• Lord Wellesley (Option 3): Introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system.

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 4): Introduced the Doctrine of Lapse and expanded railways.

question: The 1997 ____ Committee Report on Small Enterprises provided the intellectual foundation as well as a practical roadmap for this important reform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abid Hussain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1997 Abid Hussain Committee (आबिद हुसैन समिति) Report on Small Enterprises provided the intellectual foundation and a practical roadmap for reforms in the small-scale sector.

• It recommended de-reservation, abolition of investment ceilings and improved credit access for small enterprises.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Committee emphasised promoting competitiveness of small enterprises in a liberalised economy.

• Small enterprises are a major source of employment and industrial output in India.

NOTE

• P. L. Tandon (Option 1): Associated with the Tandon Committee on bank credit/working capital norms.

• K. L. Rekhi (Option 2): Not linked to this small enterprises committee report.

• Abhijit Sen (Option 3): Economist known for the committee on long-term grain policy and agriculture.

question:
"This sector of economic activities involves processing of raw materials derived from primary sector into products for sale or consumption."
Which sector of the economy is being talked about in the information given above?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secondary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Secondary sector (द्वितीयक क्षेत्र) involves the processing of raw materials derived from the primary sector into finished products for sale or consumption.

• It includes manufacturing and industrial activities such as steel making, textiles and construction.

• It is also called the industrial sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Primary sector involves extraction of natural resources (agriculture, mining, fishing).

• Value addition to raw materials is the key feature of the secondary sector.

NOTE

• Tertiary (Option 2): The service sector providing services like banking, transport and trade.

• Quaternary (Option 3): Knowledge-based services such as research, IT and consultancy.

• Quinary (Option 4): The highest-level decision-making services (top executives, policymakers).

question: Rourkela steel plant was established in ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1959.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rourkela Steel Plant (राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र) in Odisha was established in 1959.

• It was the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India.

• It was set up with technical collaboration from West Germany.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rourkela Steel Plant is now managed by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

• Other second-plan steel plants were set up at Bhilai (USSR help) and Durgapur (UK help).

NOTE

• 1954 (Option 1): Precedes the actual establishment year of the plant.

• 1969 (Option 3): Incorrect; the plant was already operational by then.

• 1985 (Option 4): Much later than the plant's actual commissioning.

question: In India, which two years were known as annual plans before eighth five year plan was launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1990-1991, 1991-1992.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The years 1990-1991 and 1991-1992 were treated as Annual Plans (वार्षिक योजना) in India.

• This gap occurred due to political instability and economic crisis before the Eighth Five Year Plan.

• The Eighth Five Year Plan was finally launched in 1992 (1992–1997).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India adopted five-year plans in 1951 under the Planning Commission.

• The Eighth Plan focused on human resource development and economic liberalisation.

NOTE

• 1969-1970, 1970-1971 (Option 1): These years fell under the plan-holiday period after the Third Plan (1966–69), not before the Eighth Plan.

• 1974-1975, 1975-1976 (Option 2): Part of the Fifth Five Year Plan period.

• 1985-1986, 1986-1987 (Option 3): Part of the Seventh Five Year Plan period.

question: The term "Current Weekly Status" in India is related to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Employment and unemployment status.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The term 'Current Weekly Status' (CWS) (वर्तमान साप्ताहिक स्थिति) is related to measuring employment and unemployment status in India.

• Under CWS, a person is considered employed if he/she works for at least one hour on any day during the reference week.

• It is used in the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) by NSSO.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other approaches include Usual Status (US) and Current Daily Status (CDS).

• The reference period for CWS is the preceding seven days.

NOTE

• Weekly rainfall measurement (Option 2): Handled by the India Meteorological Department, unrelated to CWS.

• National nutrition survey (Option 3): Deals with health and nutrition indicators, not employment.

• Parliamentary attendance reports (Option 4): Concern MPs' attendance, not labour statistics.

question:
Which of the following is consider as natural cause of population change?
I. Births
II. Migrations
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Births (जन्म) are a natural cause of population change, along with deaths.

• Migration is considered a social/artificial cause, not a natural one, as it involves movement of people between regions.

• Hence only statement I is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Population change = (Births − Deaths) + (Immigration − Emigration).

• The difference between birth rate and death rate is called the natural growth rate.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, as migration is not a natural cause.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since migration is not natural.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, since births are a natural cause.

question: What term is used for the pressure in the artery of human body during relaxation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diastolic pressure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diastolic pressure (अनुशिथिलन दाब) is the pressure in the arteries when the heart is in a state of relaxation (diastole).

• Its normal value is about 80 mm Hg.

• Blood pressure is expressed as systolic over diastolic (e.g., 120/80 mm Hg).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Blood pressure is measured using a sphygmomanometer.

• The lower (second) number in a BP reading represents the diastolic pressure.

NOTE

• Venous pressure (Option 2): The blood pressure within the veins, much lower than arterial pressure.

• Systolic pressure (Option 3): The pressure during heart contraction (systole), about 120 mm Hg.

• Capillary pressure (Option 4): Pressure within capillaries governing fluid exchange with tissues.

question: Involuntary actions like salivation and vomiting are regulated by which specific part of the hind-brain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Medulla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Medulla (मेडुला) oblongata, a part of the hind-brain, regulates involuntary actions such as salivation, vomiting, sneezing, coughing, heartbeat and breathing.

• It is also called the medulla oblongata and connects the brain to the spinal cord.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The hind-brain consists of the cerebellum, pons and medulla oblongata.

• The medulla controls vital autonomic functions essential for survival.

NOTE

• Cerebrum (Option 1): The largest part of the fore-brain, controlling voluntary actions, memory and intelligence.

• Pons (Option 2): Part of the hind-brain that acts as a bridge and helps regulate breathing rhythm.

• Hypothalamus (Option 4): Part of the fore-brain regulating temperature, hunger, thirst and hormones.

question: 'Rajagriha' was the capital city of which Mahajanapada in ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magadh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajagriha (राजगृह) (present-day Rajgir in Bihar) was the early capital of the Magadha Mahajanapada.

• Magadha later shifted its capital to Pataliputra.

• Magadha rose to become the most powerful of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajagriha was associated with rulers like Bimbisara and Ajatashatru of the Haryanka dynasty.

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha after the death of Buddha.

NOTE

• Vatsa (Option 1): Mahajanapada with its capital at Kausambi.

• Kosala (Option 2): Mahajanapada with its capital at Shravasti (and Ayodhya).

• Matsya (Option 3): Mahajanapada with its capital at Viratanagara.
